Clonotrace 1.2.1 compatibility note

Source: VERSION_REPORT_1.2.1.md

Version 1.2.1 changes one default introduced in version 1.2.0: clone-specific local rescaling is now optional and disabled by default.

The revised distance returned by clone_disance(revised = TRUE) is therefore constructed from:

  1. the raw exact-OT or approximate Clonotrace clone distance, retained up to a single global median normalization; and
  2. Euclidean distance between observed or probability-weighted clone centroids, with an optional fixed weight or a weight selected from multiresolution RNA-cluster composition.

Set local_rescale = TRUE in clone_disance() or revise_clone_distance() to reproduce the version-1.2.0 local-rescaling step. Because local rescaling can alter clone-neighbour rankings, it should be reported as a sensitivity analysis rather than treated as a change of units.

For method comparisons, retain the raw Clonotrace distance (dis_clonotrace or revised = FALSE) and report the centroid-blended distance as a separate ablation. Automatic centroid-weight selection is fate-blind but is informed by transcriptomic cluster structure; it must not be described as independent of RNA-derived state composition.

Disk-backed exact OT

Version 1.2.1 also includes the validated exact-OT backend used for the multi-dataset benchmark. build_graph_distance_store() computes cell-graph shortest-path distances in resumable row blocks and writes them to a row-major binary store. graph_clone_ot_disk() reads bounded source/target blocks from that store, calls the existing unregularized clone_2_ot() solver, balances source-clone work across a configured future plan, and writes validated per-source checkpoints.

This is a storage and execution improvement, not a new distance definition. It exactly preserves the graph-Wasserstein objective and the input clone probability masses. Its main advantages are lower peak RAM, resumability, and reuse of the expensive shortest-path calculation. The full distance store still occupies 8 * n_endpoint^2 bytes, and small jobs may run slightly more slowly than the dense in-memory implementation. Approximate distance therefore remains the routine default for large exploratory analyses.

Final validation on 2026-10-08

Validation was repeated from a clean source tarball under Ubuntu 24.04 and R 4.3.3, using one build worker and single-threaded numerical libraries to keep memory use bounded.

  • All ten R source files parsed successfully and every package in Imports was available.
  • R CMD build --no-manual completed successfully and rebuilt the vignette.
  • R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual completed with 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 3 notes. The regression suite reported 56 passes, 0 failures, and one CRAN-only smoke-test skip. The notes identify a new submission/one URL that rejects automated checks, the bundled example-data size, and an environment time-verification limitation; none indicates a runtime or API failure.
  • BiocCheck completed with 3 errors, 6 warnings, and 16 notes. Its blocking items concern Bioconductor submission policy rather than package execution: the 25 MB source tarball exceeds the Bioconductor size limit, fewer than 80% of exported man pages contain runnable examples, and the maintainer email is not registered on the Bioconductor support site. It also flags the largely non-evaluated external-data vignette, individual files over 5 MB, a concise DESCRIPTION, and style recommendations.

The package is therefore validated for the present GitHub release workflow. A formal Bioconductor submission would require a separate packaging pass to move or reduce bundled example data, expand runnable examples and vignette evaluation, and complete the maintainer-registration requirements.

The disk-backed exact-OT addition was independently revalidated on 2026-10-09. Serial and two-worker calculations matched the dense shortest-path OT result to numerical tolerance, checkpoint reuse was verified, the complete package test suite passed, the vignette compiled to HTML, and R CMD check completed with status OK.
